title: Prometheus: the fire thief
subtitle: The Titan who defies Zeus
subject: mythologie
description: Prometheus steals fire from the gods for men, then endures endless torment. A myth about progress, cunning and the price of freedom.

hero.hook: A Titan steals the fire from Olympus. Men gain civilization. He gains an eagle and a chain.

blocks.text: **Prometheus** is a Titan, a god of the previous generation. Its name evokes one who foresees. In Greek myths, he shapes the first men, protects them against **Zeus**, king of Olympus, and pays for this choice with an atrocious punishment.
By stealing fire for mortals, he gives humans technique and knowledge. His torture on the Caucasus becomes the symbol of the genius who dares to challenge power.

sections.title: Man is born naked, Prometheus trick

blocks.text: It is said that Prometheus modeled the first men with clay and water. His brother [[Epimetheus]] acts too quickly. Responsible for equipping animals, he gives everything: claws, wings, fur, speed. When the man's turn comes, there is nothing left. Humans are born fragile and defenseless.

Prometheus decides to compensate. During a sacrifice to [[Mekone]], he cuts an ox into two parts. Under an ugly skin, it hides good meat. Under appetizing fat, it hides the bones. **Zeus** chooses good looks. Since then, men have eaten the flesh and offered the bones to the gods.
To hide the fire, Prometheus uses a [[Ferule]] rod. Its marrow burns very slowly: Mediterranean shepherds really used it as a portable lighter.
Furious at having been deceived, Zeus takes away fire from men. Without heat or light, they fall back into an almost animal life.

sections.title: The theft of fire and the torture

blocks.text: Prometheus enters Olympus. He steals a spark from the chariot of the Sun, or from the forge of **Hephaestus**, god of blacksmiths, depending on the version. He hides it in his hollow stem and brings it back to mortals.

blocks.caption: Prometheus brings fire to humans, the founding act of technology.

blocks.text: For the Greeks, fire is not just a flame. He embodies **technical** and **reason**, which allows man to transform the world. Zeus retaliates. Against humanity, he will later send Pandora. Against Prometheus, the punishment is direct.
In ancient medicine, the **liver** was seen as the seat of emotions and vitality. Zeus chose this organ to break the will of the Titan.
The Titan is chained to a wall of the **Caucasus**. Every day, an eagle devours his liver. Every night, the organ is reborn. The torture begins again at dawn, without end.

For centuries, Prometheus refused to give in. He knows a dangerous secret: which woman will give birth to a son stronger than Zeus. Despite the torture, he remains silent. It becomes the symbol of resistance in the face of tyranny.

The hero **Heracles**, son of Zeus, ends up arriving in the Caucasus. He kills the eagle with an arrow and frees the prisoner. Zeus accepts the grace: Prometheus finally reveals the secret about the nymph **Thétis**. The king of the gods thus avoids his own fall.
To respect the oath that bound him to the rock, Prometheus wears a ring made from the iron of his chains and a fragment of stone. He remains “linked” to the mountain, but free.

sections.title: A myth that never goes out

blocks.text: In the 5th century BC, the tragedian [[Aeschylus]] staged “Prometheus in Chains”. Later, the myth inspires science and progress. Mary Shelley subtitles “Frankenstein” “The Modern Prometheus”: Creating life without wisdom can also destroy.

The philosopher [[Gaston Bachelard]] even speaks of a “Prometheus complex”: this desire to know more than one’s masters. Today, we often compare artificial intelligence or genetics to a new fire: an immense power, still poorly controlled.
**Prometheus** offers men civilization through the theft of fire, endures a thousand-year-old torment, then is delivered by **Heracles**. Progress has a price, and so does divine power.
